data.name: Release v2.5.1 🌈
data.body:
## 🗑️ Feature Removal Reminder

**Appsmith AI reached end of life on September 30, 2026.**

You can no longer add new Appsmith AI datasource connections or queries. Existing queries have stopped working, whether or not you have upgraded.

Migrate remaining Appsmith AI queries to a direct provider datasource, such as OpenAI, Anthropic, or Google AI.

## ⚠️ Important Upgrade Notes

- Customized `docker.env` files must now contain resolved literal values. Shell expressions stop startup with a redacted diagnostic. Move JVM options from `docker.env` to Docker Compose or Helm environment configuration before upgrading. Generated defaults and Admin Settings values need no changes. ([#42225](https://github.com/appsmithorg/appsmith/pull/42225))
- Form-based self-serve signup is now limited to 20 requests per client IP every 24 hours. Instances behind a custom proxy should ensure it sets `X-Forwarded-For`; otherwise signups can share the proxy's rate-limit bucket. Invites and super-user setup are unaffected. ([#42351](https://github.com/appsmithorg/appsmith/pull/42351))

## 🔐 Security

- Updated bundled dependencies to address reported vulnerabilities. ([#42343](https://github.com/appsmithorg/appsmith/pull/42343), [#42398](https://github.com/appsmithorg/appsmith/pull/42398))
- MongoDB smart substitution now processes large and malformed inputs in linear time while preserving valid special-type values. ([#42380](https://github.com/appsmithorg/appsmith/pull/42380))
- Application theme lists now require edit permission. Published applications continue to render with their current theme. ([#42392](https://github.com/appsmithorg/appsmith/pull/42392))
- SMTP datasource connections now enforce the restricted-host policy when testing and sending email. Existing datasources that point to blocked destinations stop connecting after upgrade. ([#42399](https://github.com/appsmithorg/appsmith/pull/42399))
- Docker environment configuration is now validated and loaded as data instead of shell code. ([#42225](https://github.com/appsmithorg/appsmith/pull/42225))
- MCP-authenticated Git requests can no longer check out remote branches or tags. Local branch workflows continue to work. ([#42414](https://github.com/appsmithorg/appsmith/pull/42414))
- Self-serve signup now has a per-client-IP rate limit. ([#42351](https://github.com/appsmithorg/appsmith/pull/42351))

## 🛠️ Reliability

- Ask AI now authorizes widget property bindings against the application instead of treating widget IDs as action IDs. ([#42383](https://github.com/appsmithorg/appsmith/pull/42383))
- Creating JS action collections concurrently no longer drops actions or fails because of a shared-list race. ([#42408](https://github.com/appsmithorg/appsmith/pull/42408))
- MCP governance audit tools can now obtain the caller's organization scope from the user profile. ([#42412](https://github.com/appsmithorg/appsmith/pull/42412))
- MCP branch creation now waits up to 120 seconds and returns the existing branch's application ID and editor URL when a retry finds that branch. ([#42413](https://github.com/appsmithorg/appsmith/pull/42413))

## ✨ New Features & Enhancements

- MCP structured SQL queries can skip empty filter values and use list-valued PostgreSQL filters. A new filter-bar recipe explains how to combine controls, queries, and events safely. ([#42373](https://github.com/appsmithorg/appsmith/pull/42373), [#42376](https://github.com/appsmithorg/appsmith/pull/42376))
- The editor now recognizes supported worker APIs such as `Blob`, `File`, `FormData`, `URL`, and text encoders without false undefined-variable errors. ([#42381](https://github.com/appsmithorg/appsmith/pull/42381))

## 🎨 UI & Widget Improvements

- Phone Input and JSON Form phone fields now keep the correct country and flag when countries share a dial code. Dial-code data for Guyana, the Cayman Islands, and Vatican City was also corrected. ([#42372](https://github.com/appsmithorg/appsmith/pull/42372))
- Legacy widgets with a **Required** toggle now show a required marker consistently. ([#42379](https://github.com/appsmithorg/appsmith/pull/42379))

## 🔧 Git, Deployment & Configuration

- Set `APPSMITH_DISABLE_HELP_ICON=true` to hide Help entry points in the editor and Applications page. The setting defaults to off. ([#42378](https://github.com/appsmithorg/appsmith/pull/42378))
- The Custom domain setting now explains the accepted format and rejects protocols, paths, and spaces before saving. ([#42405](https://github.com/appsmithorg/appsmith/pull/42405))

commit.message:
fix(server): broadcast datasource context invalidation to every pod on credential save (#42430) ## Description **TL;DR:** saving new datasource credentials now tells every backend pod of the instance to drop its cached connection for that datasource, over the Redis pub/sub channel the restart broadcast already uses. Before, only the pod that served the save rebuilt its pool, and only on its next use. ### Problem `PUT /api/v1/datasources/datasource-storages` persists the new credentials, but connection pools live per pod. `DatasourceContextServiceCEImpl.getIsStale` rebuilds a pool only on the pod that next uses it, by comparing the storage's `updatedAt` with the cached context's creation time. Every other pod keeps its pool until the 2 h idle LRU eviction, LRU pressure at 300 entries, or a restart. For JDBC plugins (HikariCP) a pool built with the old password keeps retrying connection creation forever once Hikari retires its connections at `maxLifetime`. On Appsmith Cloud, with about ten pods, a Supabase Postgres password rotation produced a failed login every 1–3 s against the customer's pooler and tripped its circuit breaker, which then rejected the correct password too. ### Change - `DatasourceContextInvalidationPublisher` publishes `{datasourceId, environmentId, pluginId}` as JSON on `datasource-context-invalidation:`. It never errors: a missing id, a missing instance id, a Redis failure or a 2 s timeout is logged and the save still succeeds. Each pod then falls back to today's lazy `getIsStale` rebuild. - `DatasourceContextInvalidationSubscriber` subscribes on `ApplicationReadyEvent` on every pod, hops off the Redis event loop to `boundedElastic`, and calls `DatasourceContextService.deleteDatasourceContext`, which destroys the connection and drops it from the context maps. Malformed or incomplete messages and failed evictions are logged and skipped; the subscription keeps running and reconnects with backoff. - `DatasourceStorageServiceCEImpl.updateDatasourceStorage` publishes after `validateAndSaveDatasourceStorageToRepository` succeeds, only for a user-originated (`isUserRefreshedUpdate == TRUE`) and persisted (`isDryOps == false`) update. The non-user path is `DatasourceContextServiceCEImpl.updateDatasourceAndSetAuthentication`, which runs right after a context is created for `UpdatableConnection` plugins; broadcasting there would evict the fresh context on every creation. - The publisher is injected through an `@Autowired` setter so the CE constructor signature stays stable for the EE subclasses that call it (`DatasourceStorageServiceCECompatibleImpl`, `DatasourceStorageServiceImpl`). No EE change is needed: EE's `DatasourceContextServiceImpl.initializeDatasourceContextIdentifier` keys contexts by `(datasourceId, environmentId)`, and the message carries both. - `DatasourceContextServiceCEImpl.deleteDatasourceContext` is hardened because the broadcast makes it run on every pod per save. It now hops to `boundedElastic` before `datasourceDestroy` (which closes the pool synchronously for MSSQL, Oracle, Snowflake, Redshift and Mongo) instead of running on the Mongo driver thread that delivered the plugin executor, and it removes only the map entries it inspected (`ConcurrentHashMap.remove(key, value)`). Before, a context rebuilt by a query while the delete awaited the executor lookup was dropped from the maps without being destroyed, leaking its pool. The publishing pod receives its own broadcast too, so it evicts immediately instead of waiting for its next use. The broadcast is sent on every user save, not only when credentials change. `DatasourceCredentialBindingResult.connectionConfigurationChanged` is computed from the public view, so a password-only rotation reports `false`; gating on it would skip the exact case this fixes. Today's `getIsStale` already treats every save as stale on every pod, so the number of pool rebuilds per save does not change, only their timing. ### Call sites checked Writers of datasource credentials: - `DatasourceServiceCEImpl.updateDatasourceStorage` (the controller path) → `DatasourceStorageServiceCEImpl.updateDatasourceStorage` with `TRUE`: **broadcasts**. - `DatasourceContextServiceCEImpl.updateDatasourceAndSetAuthentication` → same method with `FALSE`: deliberately does not broadcast (see above). - `DatasourceServiceCEImpl.updateDatasource` (`PUT /{id}`): nullifies storage fields and only saves the datasource document; no credential change. - `AuthenticationServiceCEImpl` (OAuth token exchange / refresh) and import/Git paths call `DatasourceStorageService.save` directly: out of scope. They serve plugins whose contexts are not cached (REST, GraphQL) or already rebuild lazily. ### Not done on purpose Destroying a Postgres pool on `SQLState 28P01` is not needed: `PostgresPlugin.executeCommon` already wraps any `SQLException` from `getConnectionFromHikariConnectionPool` in `StaleConnectionException`, so `retryOnce` destroys and recreates the pool on the first query that cannot get a connection. Recreation with a wrong password fails fast in `new HikariDataSource(config)` and failed creations are not cached, so no background retry survives on a pod that runs a query. Idle pods are what this PR covers. ### Known, unchanged - `getCachedDatasourceContextMono` has a microsecond window between `getIsStale` and reading the connection where a concurrent eviction can fail one query. Pre-existing for the existing `deleteDatasourceContext` callers. - `handleRemoval` (mock Mongo LRU cache only) still removes map entries unconditionally. - The new publisher/subscriber pair is a second copy of the restart pub/sub scaffold. A third consumer should extract a shared instance-scoped helper. ### Follow-ups - Shadow EE PR to verify the Spring context wires the setter through `DatasourceStorageServiceCECompatibleImpl` and to add an EE test that a message for environment X evicts only the `(datasourceId, X)` context. Fixes https://linear.app/appsmith/issue/APP-16265 ## Impact on existing instances - **Fresh install:** one more Redis pub/sub connection per pod (a dedicated `ReactiveRedisMessageListenerContainer`, as for the restart channel). No configuration. - **Upgrade from default:** same. Single-pod instances publish and receive their own message; behaviour is the existing lazy rebuild, just immediate. - **Upgrade from customized:** instances sharing one Redis across installations are isolated by the instance id in the channel name, like the restart channel. Redis unreachable: saves still succeed with at most 2 s added latency, logged at `ERROR`, and cross-pod eviction degrades to today's lazy rebuild. - **Rollback:** no persisted data or schema changes; older pods simply ignore the channel. No new env vars, Helm values or properties. ## Testing Server unit tests, all following `app/server/AGENTS.md` conventions: - `DatasourceStorageUpdateBroadcastTest` (SpringBootTest): drives `datasourceService.updateDatasourceStorage` (the controller path) and asserts the publisher receives the saved storage's datasource, environment and plugin ids. Red without the hook (`Wanted but not invoked`), green with it. Also asserts no broadcast for a non-user update or a dry run. - `DatasourceContextInvalidationPublisherTest`: channel scoping; completes empty without touching Redis when the instance id or any of the three ids is missing; the wire payload carries exactly the three id fields and no credentials; completes empty without error against an unreachable Redis. - `DatasourceContextInvalidationSubscriberTest`: evicts the context named in a valid message, also with unknown extra fields; ignores malformed or incomplete messages; completes when the eviction fails. - `DatasourceContextServiceCEImplDeleteContextTest`: `datasourceDestroy` runs on a `boundedElastic` thread; a context rebuilt while the delete awaits the executor stays cached and is not destroyed. Both red before the hardening. - `DatasourceContextInvalidationBroadcastTest` (Redis testcontainer): a publish on instance A reaches A's subscriber and evicts the right context; a publish on instance B does not. Also run locally: `DatasourceStorageServiceTest`, `DatasourceContextServiceTest`, `DatasourceServiceTest`, `InstanceRestartPublisherTest`, `InstanceRestartBroadcastTest`, `spotless:check`. Select the validation relevant to this change: - [ ] Client unit tests - [x] Server unit tests - [ ] Cypress - [ ] Playwright - [ ] Deploy preview - [ ] Not applicable ## Automation /ok-to-test tags="@tag.All" ## Communication Should the DevRel and Marketing teams inform users about this change? - [ ] Yes - [x] No 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code) > [!TIP] > 🟢 🟢 🟢 All cypress tests have passed! 🎉 🎉 🎉 > Workflow run: > Commit: 444d78317aeaf4f6230fed687051fdf8fad4a0dd > Cypress dashboard. > Tags: `@tag.All` > Spec: >
Tue, 20 Oct 2026 23:27:06 UTC ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **New Features** * Datasource updates now synchronize cached datasource contexts across application instances. * User-refreshed datasource changes automatically invalidate affected contexts, helping ensure updated configurations are used consistently. * **Bug Fixes** * Improved context cleanup to preserve newly created replacements during concurrent operations. * Invalidation and cleanup failures no longer interrupt datasource saves or leave stale contexts unnecessarily. * Prevented duplicate connection cleanup when removing cached datasource contexts. --------- Co-authored-by: Claude Fable 5.1
